verdict.delta_sentence: Compared with the nearer intent-classification-2 reference, this board offers stronger tinted phase grouping but lacks its compact visual rhythm because large dead zones and several marathon return paths fragment the composition.

sub_checks.name: frame_use
sub_checks.note: Failing: the seven phases occupy separated islands around a very large empty center, while the bottom half is mostly unused outside the isolated learning panel.

sub_checks.name: corridors_and_air
sub_checks.note: Label chips generally have clear surrounding air, and local node-to-node gaps remain comfortably readable despite the board-wide separation.

sub_checks.name: grouping
sub_checks.note: Seven labeled, lightly tinted regions clearly organize the incident lifecycle, with two or three principal nodes in most sections.

sub_checks.name: color
sub_checks.note: Distinct phase hues and green resolution paths provide useful semantics, although blue, orange, purple, and magenta routes sometimes span unrelated regions and weaken flow-family consistency.

sub_checks.name: machinery_leakage
sub_checks.note: No crosshair junctions, exposed waypoints, or orphaned badges are visible; arrowheads terminate cleanly at nodes or routed branches.

sub_checks.name: alignment_and_rhythm
sub_checks.note: Failing: individual regions are orderly, but the staggered top row, isolated center-bottom phase, and uneven section sizes produce a loose rhythm rather than a shared register.

sub_checks.name: edge_legibility
sub_checks.note: Failing: the purple preserve-timeline connection makes a very long down-and-across perimeter detour, while the blue on-call route and orange ownership route traverse broad empty areas and compete with regional boundaries.

verdict.rank_order_sanity_note: The visual ordering and assigned scores agree: gc-decomp-harness ranks first at 7.5, intent-classification-2 second at 7.0, and the board under grade third at 6.5.
